steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: Solid supports are on by default. The group has an inset (0 mm by default) and a hatch sub-group with 0.2 mm hatch distance, twice the part's 0.1 mm. The last argument false leaves out the power optimisation.
Only two patterns are offered for supports, via SUPPORT_PATTERN_KEYS: meander and offset.

lines: // On by default. support_inset (mm) shrinks the area before hatching.
// Hatch distance 0.2 mm, meander or offset only, no power optimization

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: part.support_solid holds the switch, the inset and a complete HATCH object. read_hatch is the same reader as for the part hatches, only with the support pattern list.

steps.title: Shrink the area, then hatch it
notes: process_solid_support_island is short: no border and no skin detection, only an optional inset and one call to hatch_area. The true at the end marks the vectors as support.
With 0.5 mm inset each 3 × 3 mm pillar is hatched on 2 × 2 mm only: the support touches the part on a smaller area and is easier to remove.

lines: // Optional inset (mm): keeps the support hatch away from its outline.
hatch_area(a_ctx, a_result, l_area, l_cfg.hatch, BSID.support_solid, a_ctx.island_counter,

steps.title: The offset pattern
notes: make_offset_hatch puts ring k at 0.5 · d + k · d inside the area and stops when the offset is empty. For the 2 × 2 mm area and d = 0.2 mm that gives rings at 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 mm: five rings, 20 mm per pillar.
Six pillars: 120 mm, the value ATU reports after the change. With meander and no inset it was 269.88 mm.

lines: // The first ring lies half a hatch distance inside the area border.
// Ring k lies at 0.5 * d + k * d, so neighboring rings are d apart.
// Every ring is computed from the original area (no error build-up).
let l_ring_isl = ISL.offset(a_area, -(0.5 * l_d + k * l_d));
// The rings were collected from outside to inside; inside_out reverses

steps.title: Mark the hatch as support
notes: hatch_area is shared with the part hatches: rotation angle, pattern and layer skip. Only the last line differs: support vectors get the model subtype nSubtypeSupport, which the preview, the sorting and the export use.

lines: add_hatch(a_ctx, a_result, l_res.hatch, a_bsid, a_islid, a_bounds);

steps.title: Laser settings and order
notes: Solid supports (BSID 710) run at 200 W and 1200 mm/s. Scan order 20 follows the wall supports (10) and comes before every part vector.

recipes.title: A support inset by default
recipes.why: Supports that are easier to remove, with a smaller contact area.
recipes.result: New profiles shrink every support area by 0.3 mm before hatching. Drag Inset in Try it to see the effect.

recipes.title: A coarser support hatch
recipes.why: Even less material and time for supports that only have to hold the part.
recipes.result: Support hatch lines 0.3 mm apart: a third less line length. Set the hatch distance in Try it.

recipes.title: Faster solid supports
recipes.why: Shorter build time when the supports hold well enough.
recipes.result: Solid support default 1500 mm/s. For one profile, change Scanning › Solid support › speed in the dialog instead.
